Subject: PilotBooking: initial dedicated capacity offer + activation windows

Hi Jill —

Following our call last week, attaching a pragmatic offer that maps to the traffic profile you shared (peak booking surge windows, 2s median completion SLA). High level:

- Option A: 16-GPU baseline (A100/80GB equiv), auto-burst pool to 32 for brief surges.
- Option B: 32-GPU baseline with 64-GPU staged ramp (recommended for sustained growth).
- Pricing: committed monthly runway + burst credit buffer; see attached PDF for line-item pricing and burn-rate models.

Key operational notes I want to call out:
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs (billing anchor) can be staggered across months to ease budget timing.
- We can front-load warmup (1–2 days of warm cache) to reduce initial latency risk; this is included as a one-time onboarding credit.
- Fallback: policy-based routing to smaller quantized model variants if you hit capacity during unexpected spikes.

Attachments: PB-Redwood-Dedicated-Offer-v1.pdf (proposal), PB-Redwood-Activation-Runbook.xlsx (activation milestones).

If you want, I can draft a 6–8 week activation runway with week-by-week GPU commitments and success metrics (SLOs, perf baselines, smoke tests). Next best step: procurement + legal review, then we lock the initial month-by-month commit and DocuSign.

Thanks —
Ben

Thanks Jill — answers inline below and a slightly revised offer attached (minor wording + explicit min-GPU anchors).

1) Minimum guaranteed GPUs (monthly billing anchor):
   - Option A: 8 GPUs (billed minimum) with baseline pool sized to 16 GPUs for runtime capacity; we bill at the 8-GPU reserved rate and credit burst usage above that at a discounted burst price.
   - Option B: 24 GPUs (billed minimum) with baseline pool at 32 GPUs; staged ramp commitments can be scheduled as 24 -> 32 -> 48 over months 1/3/6.

2) Regional failover:
   - Redwood supports cross-region routing. Warm failover in EU is available as a secondary pool (replicated model variant) — we recommend a 20% warm buffer (small set of nodes kept warmed) to keep failover latency under 500ms added overhead. That is an add-on line in the proposal.

3) Ramp schedule & acceptance criteria (sketch):
   - Week 0: Contract signed + slot reservation; provisioning smoke tests (synthetic traffic, model correctness) — go if smoke <2s median and no critical errors.
   - Week 1–2: Warm-up and staged traffic ramp to 25% production load; acceptance = 95th pct latency within 2.5x baseline and no >5% error rate.
   - Week 3–6: Incremental increases to 50–100% with load tests and KV cache validation; acceptance gates at 50% and 100% with documented smoke results.

SOC2: attaching a link and we can provide auditor pack under NDA — we also include an Operational Security Q&A appendix in the PDF.

Ben — quick notes from CS / Onboarding POV: 

1) Timeline: 6-week ramp is achievable if PilotBooking gives us prioritized security contacts (1 POC for legal & 1 for infra) and approves the SOC2 NDA pack in week 0. Otherwise add +2 weeks for QA scheduling.

2) Acceptance gates — recommended tweaks:
   - Gate 1 (Week 0): Provision & smoke — add a mandatory safety test (end-to-end booking simulation) and a connectivity checklist for their VPC peering.
   - Gate 2 (Week 2): 25% traffic ramp — require a perf-run of 1-hour sustained traffic at 1.5x expected peak to validate autoscaler behavior.
   - Gate 3 (Week 4): 75% traffic — require a 24-hour soak with full KV cache and user-session replication tests.

3) Min-GPU advice: we can accept a lower billed anchor (8 GPUs) only if PilotBooking allows a 30-day warmup/validation credit window where they pay at the reserved rate but we have operational permission to throttle large bursts for the first 2 weeks — that reduces their immediate Opex while protecting cluster stability. Make that explicit in the SOW.

4) EU failover: warm buffer is fine but it should be an explicit add-on priced in the proposal (runbook will call it "Regional Warm Fallback"). Onboarding will need their EU compliance POC.

I'll draft the onboarding milestones into PB-Redwood-Activation-Runbook.xlsx and attach an internal onboarding-runbook-v2.md with the checklist.

Ben / Marissa — engineering notes and concrete sizing guidance: 

- Baseline config assumptions: A100/80GB class nodes, 4 GPUs per node (network and NVLink assumptions), perf profile derived from their 512-token average prompt and 2x beam style sampling.

- Option A (cost-conservative): 
  * Billed anchor: 8 GPUs (2 nodes)
  * Runtime baseline pool: 16 GPUs (4 nodes) to hit concurrency targets.
  * Expected 95th/99th latency under normal load: ~320ms / ~520ms for short-form generation (512 tokens).
  * Warmup plan: 48-hour KV cache population job — run during week 0.

- Option B (growth): 
  * Billed anchor: 24 GPUs (6 nodes) -> staged ramp 24 -> 32 (wk3) -> 48 (wk6).
  * Expected 95th/99th latency: ~280ms / ~450ms.

- Autoscale & burst: we can enable a pre-warmed burst pool that adds +50% capacity for short duration (billing is usage-based). Recommend limiting burst windows to observed peak hours (their evening surge) to control spend.

- EU Warm Failover feasibility: yes — we can keep a 20% warm buffer (replicated model sharded) but this requires a second registry and a short replication window; operationally we can schedule this within the 6-week plan if PilotBooking provides network peering details in week 0. There is an incremental 8% monthly charge for the warm buffer.

I'll attach the onboarding-runbook-v2.md (internal) with exact infra commands and smoke-test steps. Happy to jump on a quick tech call with their infra team.

- Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
